topic: CUT: a 15-minute look at the Subscriptions page in your phone's app store account, marking apps nobody opens and canceling the easiest one
pillar: CUT: finding quiet leaks (autopay, subscriptions, things nobody uses) and how to look at them calmly.
caption:
Your phone already keeps a list of what you pay for every month.
It's the Subscriptions page in your app store account.
Write down each app, what it costs, and when it renews.
Mark the ones nobody opens. Cancel the easiest one and write down the date.
Save this for a quiet fifteen minutes this week.
The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is a good home for what you find, link in bio.
Day one counts.

slides.title: The subscriptions hiding in your phone
slides.subtitle: A calm fifteen-minute look

slides.title: Your phone keeps a list for you
slides.body: On most phones, your app store account has a page called Subscriptions. It shows what renews and when. You can do this one from the couch.

slides.title: Find the page
items: Open your app store and tap your name or photo
Look for Subscriptions in the account menu
Can't find it? Search your phone settings for subscriptions
Grab a pen and paper, or open a notes app

slides.title: Write down each one
items: What it costs and how often it charges
The last time anyone actually opened it

slides.title: The nobody-opens-it test
slides.body: Put a small mark next to anything nobody in your home opened this month. Those are your quiet leaks. If one is worth it to you, leave it alone. That counts as a decision too.

slides.title: Cancel the easiest one
slides.body: Pick one marked app and tap cancel. Read the screen, it usually tells you when access ends. Write that date down. Then close the page. One is plenty for today.

slides.title: Save it for a quiet fifteen minutes
slides.body: Want one place to write what you cut? The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is a single page. It's at my Stan store, link in bio. Day one counts.
